title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer circuit-breaker hysteresis and fallback backoff (regional stability)
author: Priya Natarajan
commits: tighten(cb): add hysteresis window and jittered backoff to fallback path
fix(race): guard double-shed case with CAS and add unit test
test(integration): add regional failover scenario to enforcer integration tests
chore(config): raise default fallback cooldown in charts/values
description:
Motivation: In recent incidents we've observed the SLO enforcer rapidly triggering regional failover and aggressive load-shedding when transient latency spikes occur. That behavior caused amplified cross-region traffic and in some cases double-shedding due to a race in the fallback path. This PR introduces a conservative hotfix intended to stabilize regional failover/fallback behavior while we iterate on longer-term throttling work.

What this changes: 1) Introduces a hysteresis window in the circuit-breaker evaluation so that short-lived violations do not immediately trigger fallback. The window is configurable and defaults to 10s. 2) Adds jittered exponential backoff to the fallback/cooldown path to prevent synchronized retries across replicas. 3) Fixes a race condition where two concurrent fallback handlers could both mark capacity as shed (double-shed) by guarding the transition with a CAS and adding an explicit state transition log. 4) Adds an integration test that simulates a regional latency spike and asserts single-failure failover with cooldown behavior. 5) Bumps the default cooldown in Helm values to be conservative for customers using default charts.

Tests and validation: Unit tests added for the circuit_breaker state machine and the CAS guard. Integration test simulates region A latency spike and verifies one fallback event and no cascade across replicas. CI initially reported a flaky integration test; root cause was a timing assumption in the test harness — adjusted sleep/await and switched to condition-based waits. All checks passed after fix.

Rollout plan: This is a hotfix intended to be rolled to production immediately via a canary to 10% of traffic with observability hooks enabled (metrics: slo_enforcer.cb_transitions, slo_enforcer.fallback_backoffs, slo_enforcer.double_shed_attempts). If metrics indicate stabilization we will promote to 100%. If any regression appears we will rollback and open a postmortem.

Related: ENG-2419 (incident follow-up), ENG-2477 (follow-on throttling RFC).
review_comments: Marco Chen: Important fix — can you add a metric for the CAS transition failure count so we can detect repeated contention?
Priya: Added slo_enforcer.cb_cas_conflicts counter; increment on CAS failure so we can monitor contention (see commit 2).
Lina Alvarez: Integration test looks sensible. Please ensure the default values bump is noted in release notes — some customers rely on short cooldowns for latency-sensitive workloads.
Priya: Added release notes entry and made cooldown configurable via values.yaml; left default conservative.
release_notes: Hotfix: Stabilize SLO enforcer fallback behavior to prevent rapid regional failovers and double-shed races. Adds hysteresis window, jittered backoff, CAS guard for fallback transitions, new telemetry, and conservative default cooldowns.
